definition: Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) searches a defined configuration space for hyperparameters that minimize a validation cost. Unlike learned model parameters, hyperparameters control the training procedure or model structure, so each trial requires training and evaluating a model.
intuition: Treat each configuration as an expensive experiment: choose a setting, train/evaluate it, learn from the result, and spend the next budget where improvement is most plausible.
mathematical_foundation:
$$
\lambda^* = \arg\min_{\lambda \in \Lambda} c(A_\lambda, D_{train}, D_{valid})
$$

`\Lambda` is the search space, `\lambda` a configuration, and `c` the validation cost of the trained model.
advantages: Can optimize mixed continuous, discrete, and conditional search spaces.
Improves a model or pipeline without requiring manual trial-and-error for every configuration.
Makes the search objective and compute budget explicit.
limitations: Results depend on the search space, budget, random seed, and evaluation protocol.
Search can be extremely expensive because every trial may require model training and validation.
Validation overfitting can occur when many configurations are tested against the same validation signal.
